classification_model.name: Bell-LaPadula classification-ceiling (carried forward unchanged from ar3_context_windows.json / sprint2_ar3_context_windows.json / sprint3_ar3_context_windows.json)
classification_model.rule: No sub-task's context window may include Zone 2 (Episodic) or Zone 5 (Entity) content bearing PII unless the sub-task itself is security-cleared. No Sprint 4 sub-task is security-cleared for raw PII read access. Where a sub-task's implementation or test reasoning needs to reference Zone 3/5 content shape, a redacted/abstract placeholder (subject/predicate/object, entity_id, attribute_name) is substituted for any real or realistic PII value -- the same discipline the design doc's own acceptance criteria and test matrix already use throughout (no example values, only abstract placeholders).
classification_model.zone_3_extension_note: Carried forward unchanged from sprint2_ar3_context_windows.json/sprint3_ar3_context_windows.json: Zone 3 (Semantic)'s relationship-fact content (SemanticEdge subject_ref/predicate/object_ref, GeneralFact.subject_scope) is treated with the same redaction caution as a Zone 2/5-adjacent zone for any item whose decisive content is real fact content rather than structural/contract shape.
classification_model.zone_7_extension_note: This story's writes ultimately land ProvenanceRecord entries in Zone 7 via the already-existing conflict-aware repositories (conflict_aware_zone_writes.py), but per sprint4_ar1_assignments.json's own p1_security_override.considered_and_not_triggered analysis, this story adds no NEW Zone 7 write path and does not touch the ZoneRepository port interface -- it only supplies call-site arguments (predicate, subject_scope, retrieval_context_hash) to already-tested repository methods. The provenance/conflict-sweep CONTRACT (per-edge provenance_id, the (entity,predicate)/(subject,predicate,object) contradiction keys) is admitted to the Dev context window; no real provenance chain content is.
classification_model.sprint_4_scope_note: Unlike Sprint 3's DASH-STORY-023/024 (a genuinely new network/credential risk class), Sprint 4's DASH-STORY-026 is pure application/API-layer wiring over already-shipped, already-tested domain primitives -- CandidateFact/classify() (Sprint-independent, pre-dating this sprint), the conflict-aware repositories (landed Sprint 3, DASH-STORY-022). No new risk class is introduced; the standard Bell-LaPadula ceiling and the design doc's own abstract-placeholder discipline (Section 5's test matrix uses |subjects|/|objects| counts, never example entity names) are sufficient here, matching sprint4_ar1_assignments.json's own p1_security_override disposition (considered, not triggered; non-blocking advisory review attached instead).
